parole.significato: The study or application of friction or rubbing as a remedy.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian anatripsologia, coined by Valeriano Luigi Brera in 1799, from Ancient Greek ἀνάτριψις (anátripsis, “rubbing”) + -λογῐ́ᾱ (-logĭ́ā).
From Italian arioso (“airy, breezy”) (from aria (“air; aria, song”) (from Ancient Greek ᾱ̓ήρ (āḗr, “air; wind”), possibly ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ews- (“dawn; east”)) + -oso) + -ose.

parole.significato: Drawings or words drawn on a surface in a public place, usually made without authorization.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Italian graffiti, from graffito, from graffire, borrowed from Ancient Greek γρᾰ́φω (grắphō, “to write”), from Proto-Hellenic *grə́pʰō, from Proto-Indo-European *gerbʰ-.

parole.significato: An informal inscription, as by a worker or vandal.
A rejected name for plutonium. (Esperium chemical symbol: Es)
parole.testo: From Italian Esperio after a Greek name of Italy + -ium, Ancient Greek Ἑσπερία (Hespería, “land of the west”).

parole.significato: A theory of evolution in which each species divides into two, only one of which develops successfully.
parole.testo: From holo- + -genesis, from Italian ologenesi, ultimately from Ancient Greek roots ὅλος (hólos, “whole”) and γένεσις (génesis, “origin, creation”).

parole.significato: A variety of grape, originally from the region of the Aegean, now used to make malmsey wine.
parole.testo: From Italian, from Ancient Greek Μονεμβασία (Monembasía, “Monemvasia”, a city on the Peloponnese), from μόνος (mónos, “only one”) + ἔμβασις (émbasis, “entering into”, ἐν + βάσις). Doublet of malvoisie.
